title: Boom Supersonic Completes First Turbine Core, Unveils 2GW Superpower Superfactory, Launches World’s Most Advanced Digital Foundry
summary: CENTENNIAL, Colo., October 22, 2026 — Boom Supersonic today unveiled its first complete supersonic turbine core, unveiled a 2GW turbine superfactory, and announced it is developing the world’s most advanced all-digital foundry, capable of casting the world’s most advanced single crystal turbine blades and vanes. The Superfactory will create up to 500 high paying jobs. The Superfactory is operational now and already making turbine parts; first single crystal components are expected to ship in 2027.
body_markdown:
Spanning nearly 200,000 square feet across two buildings in Centennial, in the South Denver area, the Superpower Superfactory represents a $150 million investment in new manufacturing capacity. A significant portion has already been spent, with investment continuing through the remaining buildout. The factory is already making parts and is expected to be fully operational by early 2027.


Starting from raw materials, the campus will manufacture blisks, blades, vanes, shafts, and cases—components representing approximately 85% of the final product by mass. Plans call for more than 75 large-format CNC and coordinate-measuring machines, with engineers, machinists, and technicians working side by side to refine designs and scale production.


Sprint Core already includes Boom-made compressor vanes, a central drive shaft, and turbine cases and frames. Keeping engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and test tightly integrated enables a small team to move rapidly from design decisions to physical hardware and real-world learning.


For critical work brought in-house, Boom can move from design changes to manufactured parts in hours or days rather than the weeks or months external supplier schedules can require. The approach gives the team direct control over quality and critical components, while allowing lessons from manufacturing and testing to flow immediately back into design.
